UNDEF phase 2 UNDEF is a global UN democracy fund which gives direct support to Civil society organissations.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2014Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The overall goal is to strengthen the voice of civil society, promote human rights and encourage the participation of all groups in democratic processes. UNDEF has achieved objectives according to the results framework. The main results from the projects are related to improved focus on women and youth participation in democratic processes. During the period 2011-2014, 129 projects were evaluated by UNDEF’s contracted commercial evaluators, Transtec. In 2014, 33 evaluations were conducted for projects mainly from Rounds Four and Five. Some 75 per cent have been deemed positive; this means that the projects were implemented above expectation or in a satisfactory way. During its 2014 Call for Project Proposals, UNDEF received 2,331 project proposals. Proposals originated from organizations in 142 countries, the vast majority local NGOs in Africa, Asia, Eastern Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean - 34 per cent of the project proposals came from Africa; 21 per cent from Europe; 19 per cent Asia, 14 per cent Latin America and 11 per cent from the Arab world. Broken down by area of focus, 30 per cent were focused on youth engagement; 19 per cent on women’s empowerment; 17 per cent on community development; 17 per cent on rule of law and human rights; 7 per cent on strengthening interaction with government; 6 per cent on media and 3 per cent on tools for knowledge. The shrinking or closing space for democracy was a challenge that persisted and even increased in 2014, impacting more countries and adversely affecting UNDEF’s capacity to implement projects in those countries. In order to achieve the overall goal, in 2014 UNDEF initiated 49 new projects reaching some 55 countries.
